claim: Iter 136 JOB A P8 calibration audit at realistic (downsampled) positive rates (1.44%, 1.00%, 0.50%, 0.10%, 0.05%) on XGB-20raw and XGB-24full (n_estimators=180, max_depth=5, lr=0.1, scale_pos_weight=69 from n_neg/n_pos=69) vs 3 cohorts (v_mean quintile, Amount quintile synthesized as rank(V_std), Time tertile synthesized as rank(V_max)) and 2 cal methods (raw, iso_per_cohort). H1 PASS — RAW worst-cohort ECE is ROBUST to positive rate: span 0.166-0.218 (XGB-20raw, 3 cohorts × 5 rates); iter-99 hot-spot persists at every rate. H2 PASS — DECISIVE: per-cohort isotonic AMPLIFIES worst-cell ECE to >= 0.99 on most cohort × tree cells at rates <= 1.0% (XGB-20raw amount iso worst-ECE: 0.985->0.984->0.994->0.998->0.865 across 5 rates). Mean global ECE jumps from 0.13 (raw) to 0.92 (iso) at rate=0.5% — a 7x AMPLIFICATION. H3 PASS — iter-99 worst hot-spot (Amount Q0 XGB-20raw ECE=0.176) DOES NOT close at low rates under raw (0.218 at rate=0.05%) and AMPLIFIES under iso (0.865 at rate=0.05%). H4 PASS — at production fraud-ops rates (0.05%-0.50%), per-cohort isotonic recommendation is INVALID; iter-104 finding reframed: per-cohort PAVA requires N_per_cohort~30 positives to support isotonic estimation; at production rates that's too few. Operational: (a) DO NOT deploy per-cohort isotonic at production fraud rates <= 1.0%; (b) RAW + global rate-rescaler preserves rank and avoids iso amplification disaster; (c) add rate-stratified isocalibration audit as standard P8 protocol. Cross-paper coupling: (i) iter-99 row 93 (release-rate ECE audit, anchor); (ii) iter-104 row 117 (per-cohort iso at release; DOWNGRADED by iter-136 at low rates); (iii) iter-12 row 22 (PR-AUC realistic rates; tells DIFFERENT story from calibration — PR-AUC rank-preserves while iso ECE amplifies); (iv) iter-132 row 147 (mislabel-noise; complementary production-fidelity perturbation); (v) P5P8-SYNTH iter-136 row 152 JOB B (D5 = iso ECE>0.10 density = 100% at all rates); (vi) FRONTIER INSIGHTS Round 2 (ZVF = signal availability; per-cohort PAVA requires observed positives — at production rates < 30/cohort, too few). paper_P8_fraud.pdf rebuilds to 59 pages / 0 errors / 0 undefined citations (was 56, +3 pages from sec:p8-iter136-cal-realistic and sec:synth-iter136-five-domain-density). Pre-existing build error fixed: synth_iter132_four_domain_density.tex referenced non-P8 label sec:p7-iter131-per-prompt-adaptive-gstar — retargeted to descriptive reference.

claim: Iter 136 JOB B P5P8-SYNTH five-domain density matrix (closes iter-132 mint vein #1). Adds D5 = P8 per-cohort ECE>0.10 density under iso_per_cohort at the realistic 0.5% positive rate (26/26 = 100.0%, CI [1.000,1.000]) alongside D1=P8 grad-band 0.84%, D2=P7 zvf-triage-step 50.0%, D3=P5 mega zvf=1.0 36.7%, D4=P7 per-prompt boundary 72.9%. H1 PASS — D5 = 100% ECE violation density at every positive rate {0.05,0.10,0.50,1.00,1.44}% (rate-independent). H2 PASS — iter-124 super-domain split {P5,P7-step} <-> P8 SURVIVES: D1/D2=0.017, D1/D3=0.023, D1/D4=0.012, D1/D5=0.008 — all 4 ratios EXCLUDE 1.0 by 50x-100x. H3 PASS — P8 super-domain has 119x internal heterogeneity (D1=0.84% vs D5=100%); reports aggregating P8 density without specifying domain are misleading. H4 PASS — density rank monotonic in granularity: D5 (>cohort-cell) > D4 (>prompt-cell) > D2 (>step) > D3 (>cell) > D1 (row). Operational: (a) cross-pillar density rhetoric must specify the domain; (b) D5 is the empirical upper bound on calibration violation density; (c) within P8 super-domain, density-regime distinction is sharper than iter-124 acknowledged.
